svg.title: Ordinal endpoint, dense translated orbit and failure of compact extraction
svg.desc: Exact symbolic diagram for the embedding of the compact ordinal interval into the torus with uncountably many coordinates. A positive weighted sum of translates has full support, but a compact subset avoiding every translated endpoint pulls back to bounded null ordinal sets.

g.text: Dense orbit and full support do not imply compact extraction
Exact symbolic objects; the torus X = T^[0,ω₁) is compact Hausdorff and separable.
Compact ordinal interval Z = [0,ω₁]
ν̄({ω₁}) = 0; every endpoint tail has measure 1.
C compact, ω₁ ∉ C ⇒ C bounded ⇒ ν̄(C) = 0.
countable ordinals
ω₁
Embedded copy D = F(Z) ⊂ X
F(t)ᵢ = 0 if t < i+1; F(t)ᵢ = ½ if t ≥ i+1.
p = F(ω₁); pᵢ = ½ in every coordinate.
L compact, p ∉ L ⇒ λ(L) = 0.
F
Translate by a = (αᵢ mod 1); {1,αᵢ} are rationally independent.
τₙ(x) = x+na; μ = Σₙ cₙ (τₙ)*λ; cₙ = 2^−|n| / 3; Σₙ cₙ = 1.
{p+na : n ∈ Z} is countable and dense. Every nonempty open U has μ(U) > 0.
The action is continuous, free, quasi-invariant and ergodic. Proof: Proposition 1.2; Theorem 3.1.
E = X \ {p+na : n ∈ Z} is Borel and conull, μ(E) = 1.
L ⊂ E compact ⇒ F^−1(τ₋ₙL) bounded for every n ⇒ λₙ(L) = 0 ⇒ μ(L) = 0.
This Borel space is not standard: null singletons cannot support its 0–1 conditional probabilities.
